reply_text:
I’d fix these two issues before merging:

1. **[P1] Printed prices are 100× too high** — `receipt/render.py:2`
   `format_money` formats cents directly as dollars. For example, `format_money(1299)` returns `$1299.00` instead of `$12.99`; two coffees at 450 cents print as `$900.00` instead of `$9.00`. Convert cents to dollars before formatting. Add assertions against literal expected strings—the current test uses `format_money` to verify itself, so it misses this.

2. **[P2] The right-alignment helper isn’t used by the renderer** — `receipt/render.py:7`
   `render_line` pads the name to 20 characters but doesn’t align the amount’s right edge. Different-length prices therefore end in different columns rather than at the intended 32-character boundary. Use `align(name, formatted_total)` and test rendered lines with different-length amounts.

All **3 existing tests pass**, but they don’t catch these issues. Reviewed local `receipt-lines` (`a6c40d4`) against `main` (`93ab743`). No files changed.
